caption: Fig. 1: Multiple BS-collected MIMO channel-position observations from the same RF environment are encoded into a wireless world embedding, which provides environment-level conditioning for downstream wireless and RF-observable inference tasks.

Fig. 2: Channel2World architecture. Path tokens from context channel-position pairs are aggregated through attention into wireless world embedding tokens, which condition query-side position and gain prediction heads.
Fig. 3: Pretraining and downstream protocol. The encoder is pretrained with context-query channel sets and then frozen for task-specific downstream learning.
Fig. 4: Ray-tracing factory dataset. A one-dimensional BS grid and a dense two-dimensional UE grid generate BS-centered propagation environments for each layout.
Fig. 5: Pretraining validation curves for position GMM loss and relative gain RMSE under error-aware and error-free inputs.
Fig. 6: Per-path UE-position GMMs for a query path in a test environment.
Fig. 7: Cosine similarity between wireless world embeddings obtained from nearby BSs in the same factory layout.
Fig. 8: Channel matrix-to-position estimation in test environments. Position RMSE is shown versus the number of downstream-model parameters.
Fig. 9: Beam-domain CSI reconstruction RMSE from sparse codebook measurements in test environments.

Fig. 10: RF-observable geometry reconstruction from NLoS path directions. Predicted interaction points are shown using embeddings inferred by the error-aware encoder with 128 128 context channels and by the error-free encoder with 1024 1024 context channels.
